name: Lucid Motors
desc: Makes luxury electric cars, including the Lucid Air sedan and Gravity SUV, and supplies powertrain technology to other carmakers.
markets: Sells in the US, Canada, Europe and the Gulf; factories in Arizona and Saudi Arabia; Public Investment Fund is majority owner.
rationale: Premium technology brand seeking global awareness among affluent buyers; F1 offers Gulf and European exposure plus a showcase for efficiency technology.

name: Rivian
desc: Makes electric pickups, SUVs and delivery vans for consumers and fleets, with Amazon as its main commercial customer.
markets: Sells in the United States and Canada; factory in Illinois with a Georgia plant planned; software joint venture with Volkswagen.
rationale: North American adventure brand with limited overseas presence; F1 could raise awareness among younger buyers but its customers are mostly in North America.

name: Stellantis
desc: Builds and sells cars and light commercial vehicles under brands including Jeep, Ram, Fiat, Peugeot, Opel, Alfa Romeo and Maserati.
markets: Sells in more than 130 markets across Europe, North America, South America, the Middle East, Africa and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: Multi-brand automaker with large European and US sales and several performance brands; clear fit for global brand building and dealer and fleet hospitality.
changed: Formed in 2021 by the merger of Fiat Chrysler and PSA Group

name: AutoCanada
desc: Operates franchised new and used car, truck and collision businesses in Canada, plus parts, service, finance and insurance products.
markets: Dealerships across Canada only; no verified expansion plans outside Canada.
rationale: Canadian retail dealer group with local marketing; little reason to buy global F1 rights, though a dealer-network hospitality angle is possible.

name: Carvana
desc: Sells used cars online with home delivery or pickup from car vending machines, and finances and buys vehicles from customers.
markets: Customers across the United States only; no verified international expansion plans.
rationale: Heavy consumer advertiser with a strong digital brand; F1 offers US audience growth but costs are large relative to its single-country business.

name: Faraday Future
desc: Develops premium electric vehicles such as the FF 91 and is moving into embodied AI robotics.
markets: Based in California with very few vehicle deliveries so far; no verified international sales.
rationale: Cash-constrained, with very low sales; F1 might help technology and robotics visibility, but a major sponsorship budget is unlikely.

name: Group 1 Automotive
desc: Runs about 130 franchised car dealerships and collision centers in the United States and the United Kingdom.
markets: Dealerships in the United States and United Kingdom; no other verified countries.
rationale: Dealer group with US and UK customers, some of them F1 markets; hospitality could suit customer events, but retail marketing budgets are modest.

name: Leapmotor
desc: Sells compact electric and range-extender cars such as the T03, C10 and B10, with Stellantis handling sales outside China.
markets: Chinese maker; sells in China and, through Leapmotor International with Stellantis, in Europe and other markets from Hoofddorp.
rationale: Budget EV brand growing in Europe through Stellantis dealers; F1 could build recognition in Europe but its price-led positioning limits the fit.
changed: Stellantis took a stake of about 21 percent and formed Leapmotor International in 2023

name: O'Reilly Auto Parts
desc: Retails automotive replacement parts, tools and accessories to do-it-yourself customers and professional service providers.
markets: Stores in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
rationale: Large North American parts retailer with motorsport-adjacent customers, but a domestic retail focus makes a global F1 deal hard to justify.

name: Sila
desc: Produces silicon-based anode material to replace graphite in lithium-ion batteries and increase energy density for electric vehicles.
markets: Production in Washington state; supplies battery makers and carmakers; no verified plans for plants abroad.
rationale: B2B materials supplier with no consumer brand; F1 could serve as a technology showcase but spend would be hard to justify.

name: Volkswagen Group
desc: Makes cars, trucks and motorcycles under Volkswagen, Audi, Porsche, Skoda, SEAT, Cupra, Bentley, Lamborghini, Scania, MAN and Ducati.
markets: Sells vehicles in Europe, North America, South America and Asia, with China as a very large market.
rationale: Already in F1 through Audi, which runs a works team; group brands could use the platform for technology and brand marketing.
f1: Owns Audi, which runs the Audi F1 works team from 2026

name: NIO
desc: Sells premium electric cars under the NIO, ONVO and firefly brands, with battery-swapping stations and a strong owner community.
markets: Sells in China and in several European countries; battery-swap network in China and some European markets.
rationale: Premium EV brand building global awareness and an owner community; F1 could support its European expansion, though it is still loss-making.

name: BYD Company
desc: Makes battery-electric and plug-in hybrid cars under BYD, Denza and Yangwang, plus buses, trucks, batteries and electronics components.
markets: Sells in China, Europe, Latin America, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, with new plants abroad.
rationale: The world leading maker of new energy vehicles with strong overseas growth; F1 offers global brand reach among European and Asian buyers.

name: Cummins
desc: Designs and makes diesel, natural gas, electric and hydrogen engines, powertrains, generators, filtration and emissions systems.
markets: Sells engines and power systems to truck, construction, mining, rail and power customers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B power technology firm that could use F1 for engineering credibility and customer hospitality; little consumer branding makes the case moderate.

name: Forvia
desc: Supplies car makers with seating, interiors, clean mobility, lighting, electronics and lifecycle solutions.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia, serving most major carmakers.
rationale: B2B automotive supplier with technology to show to carmakers; F1 hospitality may suit customer relations, but brand awareness is limited.
changed: Faurecia acquired Hella and became Forvia in 2022

name: Nissan Motor
desc: Sells Nissan, Infiniti and Datsun vehicles, including the Leaf, Ariya, Qashqai and GT-R, in partnership with Renault and Mitsubishi.
markets: Sells in Japan, North America, Europe, China and other Asian markets, with a long-standing alliance with Renault and Mitsubishi.
rationale: Global car brand with performance heritage and a strong electrification story; F1 offers worldwide visibility, though it is restructuring.

name: Valeo
desc: Produces driver-assistance sensors, lighting, thermal systems, powertrain electrification and interior controls for carmakers.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, North America and Asia supplying most major carmakers.
rationale: B2B supplier with technology in sensors and electrification that could be showcased; hospitality value for carmaker customers, but low consumer awareness.

name: XPENG
desc: Sells smart electric cars such as the G6, G9, P7+ and Mona models and develops flying cars and humanoid robots.
markets: Sells in China and in Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia; also develops flying vehicles and robots.
rationale: Technology-led EV brand expanding in Europe and Asia; F1 offers a global stage for its driver-assistance and AI credentials.

name: Polestar
desc: Sells electric performance cars, the Polestar 2, 3, 4 and 5, to consumers online and through retail spaces.
markets: Sells in over 25 markets across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific; majority-owned by Geely.
rationale: Performance-focused EV brand with design and technology credentials and global ambitions; F1 fits its premium positioning and need for awareness.

name: TE Connectivity
desc: Makes connectors, sensors and harnesses for car makers, industrial automation, aerospace, medical, energy and data-center customers.
markets: Sells to customers in more than 130 countries, with factories and engineering centres across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: B2B component supplier that could show sensor and connector technology to motorsport and automotive customers; limited consumer branding.

name: Alkegen
desc: Makes engineered materials such as battery and thermal protection materials, filtration media, fibre insulation and silicon anode materials.
markets: Customers are automakers, industrial, energy and consumer product companies; backed by private equity firm Altus Capital Partners.
rationale: B2B materials supplier with technical products relevant to EV batteries and thermal management; F1 hospitality might help, but brand awareness is low.

name: Ola Electric
desc: Makes electric scooters such as the S1 and is building motorbikes and its own battery cells in Tamil Nadu.
markets: Sells mainly in India; no verified expansion plans beyond the home market.
rationale: Strong consumer brand in India, a growing F1 audience, but sales are domestic and the business is loss-making.

name: Eaton Corporation
desc: Makes electrical equipment such as switchgear and circuit breakers, plus hydraulics, aerospace fuel systems and vehicle components.
markets: Sells to industrial, utility, data-center, aerospace and vehicle customers in more than 150 countries.
rationale: B2B power management firm with data-center and electrification exposure; F1 could provide technology showcase and customer hospitality at modest brand value.

name: Aptiv
desc: Develops vehicle architecture, active safety and driver-assistance software, connectivity and electrical systems for car makers.
markets: Engineering and manufacturing sites and customers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B technology supplier that could show safety and software capabilities to carmakers; hospitality value moderate, consumer awareness limited.
changed: Announced a planned spin-off of its electrical distribution business in 2025

name: Aurora
desc: Develops the Aurora Driver self-driving system for long-haul trucks and has started driverless trucking operations.
markets: Driverless truck operations in Texas; customers are US freight and trucking companies; no verified overseas plans.
rationale: Autonomous driving specialist selling to freight companies; F1 offers a technology showcase, but its customers are in the US only.

name: Automotive Cells Company
desc: Builds lithium-ion battery gigafactories to supply electric cars, owned jointly by Stellantis, Mercedes-Benz and Saft.
markets: First plant in northern France, with further sites planned in Germany and Italy; customers are its shareholders and other carmakers.
rationale: B2B battery joint venture with no consumer brand; F1 interest would depend on shareholders, with limited standalone commercial logic.
f1: Co-owned by Mercedes-Benz, an F1 team owner and engine supplier

name: BAIC BluePark
desc: Makes electric cars, including the ARCFOX premium brand, as the electric vehicle arm of Beijing Automotive Group.
markets: Sells mainly in China; state-controlled and loss-making in recent years; limited verified export sales.
rationale: State-controlled EV brand with modest awareness and weak finances; F1 might help ARCFOX positioning but a large budget looks unlikely.

name: Hozon
desc: Sold affordable electric SUVs and hatchbacks under the Neta brand, mainly in China and Southeast Asia.
markets: Sold in China and Southeast Asia; ran into severe cash problems in 2024 and entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2025.
rationale: Financially distressed EV maker in restructuring; a sponsorship deal is very unlikely.

name: Nikola Motor Company
desc: Developed battery-electric and hydrogen fuel cell heavy trucks, but ceased operations after its 2025 bankruptcy.
markets: Sold trucks mainly in the United States before collapsing; no ongoing operations.
rationale: Company has failed and has no ongoing business or marketing budget; not a viable prospect.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in February 2025 and wound down

name: StarPlus Energy
desc: Builds electric vehicle battery plants in Indiana as a joint venture between Stellantis and Samsung SDI.
markets: Battery plants in Kokomo, Indiana, supplying Stellantis vehicles in North America.
rationale: Joint-venture battery manufacturing vehicle with no consumer brand; very weak F1 fit.

name: T3 Travel
desc: Runs a ride-hailing app in Chinese cities using company-owned electric vehicles, backed by FAW, Dongfeng and Changan.
markets: Operates in dozens of Chinese cities; no verified operations or expansion plans outside China.
rationale: Consumer ride-hailing app with a domestic audience and automaker backers; limited international profile makes F1 an unlikely priority.

name: ABC Technologies
desc: Makes plastic components and systems for the automotive industry, including air induction and fluid handling parts.
markets: B2B supplier to carmakers; Crunchbase describes it as global; specific plants and customers not confirmed here.
rationale: B2B parts supplier with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality could help customer relations but the commercial case is thin.

name: Adient
desc: Designs and makes car seats, including structures, foam, trim and fabrics, as the largest automotive seating supplier.
markets: Plants and customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia supplying most major carmakers.
rationale: B2B supplier with deep carmaker relationships; F1 could offer hospitality for customers and a showcase of seating technology, but brand awareness is low.

name: Advance Auto Parts
desc: Retails automotive aftermarket parts such as batteries, brakes, filters, oil and accessories to do-it-yourself and professional customers.
markets: Stores in the United States and Canada, with no verified expansion plans elsewhere.
rationale: Recognised North American parts brand; F1 offers consumer exposure but its customer base is in the US and Canada only.

name: America's Car-Mart
desc: Sells affordable used vehicles and provides in-house financing to customers across the United States.
markets: Dealerships in the United States only; no verified plans abroad.
rationale: Domestic subprime-oriented used car dealer with local advertising; weak fit with a global F1 audience.

name: AUTO1 Group
desc: Runs a wholesale and online used car trading platform in Europe, with the Autohero brand for retail sales.
markets: Trades used cars across Europe; Autohero retail operates in several European countries.
rationale: Brand-led used car platform with strong marketing across Europe; F1 could extend Autohero awareness in European markets.

name: Autohome
desc: Operates a Chinese online automotive platform with car pricing, reviews, dealer listings and used car transactions.
markets: Users and advertisers are mainly in China; no verified overseas operations.
rationale: Large Chinese car-shopping platform with advertising revenue; F1 interest would be limited by its domestic audience.

name: Avatr
desc: Sells premium smart electric cars, the Avatr 11, 12 and 07, developed with Changan Automobile, CATL and Huawei.
markets: Sells in China and has started exporting; Changan, CATL and Huawei are partners and investors.
rationale: Premium smart EV brand with international ambitions; F1 could build awareness outside China, though it is young and still scaling.

name: Bombardier Recreational Products
desc: Makes recreational vehicles under the Sea-Doo, Ski-Doo, Can-Am off-road and on-road, Lynx and Evinrude brands.
markets: Sells powersports vehicles in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America through dealer networks.
rationale: Consumer powersports brands with performance image and worldwide dealers; F1 could suit premium customer hospitality and brand exposure.

name: EVgo
desc: Operates public direct current fast charging stations for electric vehicles across the United States.
markets: Charging stations in the United States only; no verified international plans.
rationale: Domestic charging operator; F1 could signal EV technology credentials, but the audience is mostly outside its US footprint.

name: Geely Holding Group
desc: Owns Chinese and international car brands including Volvo Cars, Polestar, Lotus, Zeekr and Lynk & Co, plus other businesses.
markets: Brands sold in China, Europe, North America and other markets; founded 1986 and privately held by Li Shufu.
rationale: Multi-brand group with premium and performance names and global expansion; strong fit for F1 brand building and hospitality.

name: Jaguar Land Rover
desc: Makes Jaguar, Land Rover, Range Rover and Defender vehicles for premium and luxury customers worldwide.
markets: Sells in the UK, Europe, North America, China and other markets; owned by Tata Motors.
rationale: Premium UK brands with global reach and high-net-worth customers; F1 fits hospitality and brand goals, though Jaguar competes in Formula E.
changed: Tata Motors demerged in 2025; JLR sits in the passenger vehicle company

name: Magna International
desc: Supplies car makers with body structures, seating, mirrors, powertrain systems and contract vehicle assembly.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B supplier that could use F1 for customer hospitality and engineering showcase; low consumer visibility.

name: Shriram Finance
desc: Lends to small truck operators for used commercial vehicles and offers other loans through thousands of branches in India.
markets: Customers in India only; no verified overseas expansion plans.
rationale: Niche Indian lender known to truckers; F1 offers little relevance to its rural and transport customer base.
changed: Merged with Shriram City Union Finance and renamed Shriram Finance in 2022

name: Boyd Group Services
desc: Operates collision repair shops under the Gerber Collision & Glass brand in North America.
markets: Repair centers in Canada and the United States.
rationale: Local collision repair chain with insurer customers; weak F1 fit beyond some regional awareness.

name: Ather Energy
desc: Makes Ather 450 and Rizta electric scooters, runs a fast-charging network and develops its own software.
markets: Sells through experience centres across India; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Premium Indian e-scooter brand with technology focus; F1 could raise awareness with urban buyers, but sales are domestic.

name: Geely Automobile Holdings
desc: Makes cars under the Geely, Lynk & Co and Zeekr brands, as the main listed vehicle arm of Geely Holding.
markets: Sells in China and exports to Europe, the Middle East, Latin America and Asia.
rationale: Listed car maker with growing overseas sales and premium brands; F1 could build international awareness for Lynk & Co and Zeekr.

name: H.B. Fuller
desc: Makes industrial adhesives, sealants and coatings used in packaging, electronics, automotive, construction and other industries.
markets: Sells adhesives to industrial customers in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia-Pacific.
rationale: B2B adhesives supplier; F1 offers a technology and customer hospitality platform, but little consumer brand awareness.

name: Shenzhou Automotiv Techg
desc: Chinese company in Wuhan that develops and sells automotive technology and vehicles, according to Crunchbase; details unconfirmed.
markets: Based in Wuhan, China; customers and products not confirmed; no verified international activity.
rationale: Little verified information; a small Chinese automotive technology firm with no known marketing activity or global brand.

name: The Goodyear Tire & Rubber
desc: Makes tires under the Goodyear, Dunlop and Cooper brands for consumers, fleets and carmakers.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific and Latin America through dealers, retail and carmaker supply.
rationale: Global tire brand with motorsport heritage and a consumer brand; strong potential fit for F1 hospitality and brand marketing.

name: Traton
desc: Holds the commercial vehicle businesses of Volkswagen Group, including Scania, MAN, International and Volkswagen Truck & Bus.
markets: Sells trucks and buses in Europe, North America and Latin America; majority-owned by Volkswagen Group.
rationale: B2B truck maker with brands like Scania; F1 could suit group hospitality, with Volkswagen already invested in F1 through Audi.
f1: Majority-owned by Volkswagen Group, owner of the Audi F1 works team

name: Digital Currency X Technology
desc: Chinese company in Jilin that develops and makes electric vehicle products, according to Crunchbase; details unconfirmed.
markets: Based in Jilin, China; no verified customers, products or international activity.
rationale: Little verified information; name suggests a possible former or alternate name, with no clear brand or F1 case.

name: ECARX
desc: Supplies smart cockpit systems, infotainment, compute platforms and software to carmakers such as Geely, Lynk & Co, Volvo and Polestar.
markets: Chinese automotive technology supplier with research sites in China and Europe; customers are mainly Geely group brands.
rationale: B2B supplier with limited public awareness; F1 could showcase in-car technology to carmakers, but spend would be hard to justify.

name: Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies
desc: Co-develops software and electrical architecture for electric vehicles as a joint venture of Rivian and Volkswagen Group.
markets: Joint venture based in California serving Rivian and Volkswagen Group vehicles, targeting Volkswagen cars from 2027.
rationale: Technology joint venture with no consumer brand of its own; very weak standalone F1 fit.
f1: Co-owned by Volkswagen Group, owner of the Audi F1 works team

name: VinFast
desc: Makes electric vehicles including the VF 3, VF 5, VF 6, VF 7, VF 8 and VF 9.
markets: Sells in Vietnam and in the United States, Canada, Europe and several Asian markets.
rationale: Fast-expanding EV brand seeking global visibility; F1 could raise awareness in overseas markets despite heavy losses.

name: BlueOval SK
desc: Produces electric vehicle batteries for Ford as a joint venture between Ford Motor Company and South Korea SK On.
markets: Battery plants in Tennessee and Kentucky supplying Ford vehicles in the United States.
rationale: Battery plant joint venture with no consumer brand; weak F1 fit despite Ford ownership.
changed: Ford and SK On agreed to split the joint venture in late 2025
f1: Co-owned by Ford, which partners with Red Bull Ford Powertrains in F1

name: Ally Financial
desc: Provides auto loans and leases through dealers, plus online banking, mortgages and insurance products in the United States.
markets: Customers and dealers in the United States only.
rationale: US auto lender and digital bank with brand marketing; F1 audience is mostly outside its single-country market.

name: Autoliv
desc: Makes airbags, seatbelts and steering wheels, as the largest automotive safety supplier in the world.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia supplying most carmakers.
rationale: B2B safety supplier whose brand ties closely with motorsport safety themes; F1 could help customer hospitality, though consumer awareness is low.

name: Fisker
desc: Was an electric vehicle maker that sold the Ocean SUV, built by Magna Steyr in Austria.
markets: Sold the Ocean in the United States and Europe before collapsing; no ongoing operations.
rationale: Company went bankrupt in 2024 and no longer operates; not a viable prospect for sponsorship.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in June 2024

name: Icahn Enterprises
hq: Sunny Isles Beach, Florida, United States
desc: Diversified holding company controlled by Carl Icahn, with investment, energy, automotive, food packaging and real estate segments.
markets: US-focused holding company; operating businesses and investments mostly in the United States.
rationale: Diversified holding with no unified consumer brand; F1 offers little strategic fit.

name: Volvo Cars
desc: Makes Volvo premium cars, including the XC90, XC60, EX30 and EX90, known for safety and Scandinavian design.
markets: Sells in Europe, North America and Asia including China; majority-owned by Geely Holding.
rationale: Premium brand with safety and electrification positioning and global customers; F1 offers European and US exposure, though it has not been a motorsport-led marque.

name: Zhiji Auto (IM Motors)
desc: Sells premium electric cars under the IM brand, backed by SAIC Motor, Zhangjiang Hi-Tech and Alibaba.
markets: Sells mainly in China; brand is backed by SAIC Motor and partners; limited verified overseas sales.
rationale: State-backed premium EV brand with limited awareness outside China; F1 could help global positioning but its scale is modest.

name: FAW Pentium
desc: Sells Bestune sedans and SUVs, including the T77, T99 and NAT electric models, under state-owned FAW Group.
markets: Sells mainly to consumers in China, with some exports; limited recognition abroad.
rationale: Mid-market state-owned brand with little international recognition; F1 offers modest value for its mostly domestic business.

name: IONITY
desc: Operates a high-power charging network for electric vehicles across Europe with over 5,000 charging points.
markets: Charging sites along European highways; shareholders are carmakers and investment firm BlackRock.
rationale: European charging brand with carmaker shareholders and technology angle; F1 could raise awareness in European markets.
f1: Co-owned by Mercedes-Benz, Ford and Volkswagen Group, all linked to F1

name: Renault Group
desc: Sells Renault, Dacia and Alpine cars and light commercial vehicles, including electric models.
markets: Sells in Europe, Latin America, Africa, the Middle East and Asia, with a long-standing alliance with Nissan.
rationale: Established F1 participant through Alpine; group uses motorsport for performance branding across global markets.
f1: Owns Alpine, which runs the Alpine F1 Team

name: ZF Group
desc: Supplies transmissions, chassis systems, driver assistance, electric drives and commercial vehicle technology to carmakers.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia; owned mainly by a foundation.
rationale: B2B technology supplier with engineering strengths and carmaker customers; F1 hospitality could help, though consumer awareness is low.

name: Electra
desc: Operates ultra-fast electric vehicle charging stations in France, Belgium and Italy, with a pay-as-you-go app and subscription.
markets: Charging stations in France, Belgium, Italy and other European countries; backed by Eurazeo, EDF and others.
rationale: European charging operator with a technology angle; F1 reach is large relative to its regional customer base.

name: Erisha E Mobility
desc: Indian electric vehicle maker based in New Delhi, said by Crunchbase to provide electric vehicles; details unconfirmed.
markets: Based in New Delhi; no verified products, customers or international activity.
rationale: Little verified information; no known marketing activity or global brand to support an F1 case.

name: First Brands Group
desc: Makes aftermarket auto parts under brands including Fram filters, Autolite spark plugs, Trico wipers and Raybestos brakes.
markets: Sells through US retailers such as AutoZone and Advance, and to installers; some international business.
rationale: Well known consumer parts brands, but the company is in bankruptcy and unlikely to fund a sponsorship.
changed: Filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in September 2025

name: GridServe
desc: Operates the GridServe Electric Highway fast charging network on UK motorways, electric forecourts, and solar and battery farms.
industry: electric vehicle charging and energy company
markets: Operates in the United Kingdom only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: UK charging and renewable energy firm; F1 fits its EV profile, but its operations and customers are domestic.

name: Lithia & Driveway
desc: Operates more than 400 franchised car stores and the Driveway online retail brand in the United States, Canada and UK.
markets: Franchised stores in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom.
rationale: Large dealer group with an online brand; F1 hospitality could suit customer events, but retail marketing is mostly local.

name: XCMG Automobile
desc: Makes heavy trucks, special-purpose vehicles and truck mixers in China as the automotive division of XCMG Group.
markets: Sells mainly in China; parent XCMG exports construction machinery widely, but the truck division footprint is unconfirmed.
rationale: B2B commercial vehicle maker with little consumer awareness; F1 hospitality might suit its parent, but the fit is weak.

name: ElectroMobility Poland
desc: State-owned company developing the Izera electric car brand and a factory in Jaworzno, Silesia.
markets: Based in Poland; owners are Polish state energy and industry firms; car launch repeatedly delayed.
rationale: State-backed national project with no car on sale yet; F1 offers little commercial benefit.

name: Gogoro
desc: Makes Smartscooters and runs a battery-swapping network for electric scooter riders, mainly in Taiwan.
markets: Sells mainly in Taiwan, with partners selling scooters and swapping in India, China and Southeast Asia.
rationale: Technology-led two-wheeler brand with Asian growth plans; F1 could help awareness in Asia, but its finances are modest.

name: Aeva
desc: Develops 4D lidar sensors using frequency-modulated continuous-wave technology that measure distance and velocity for vehicles and industry.
markets: Works with automotive and industrial customers and partners in the United States, Europe and Asia.
rationale: Technology supplier that could use F1 as a sensor showcase for carmakers, but its brand is B2B and small.

name: Empery Digital
desc: Former electric off-road powersports maker Volcon that pivoted in 2025 to a bitcoin treasury strategy.
markets: US-based Nasdaq-listed company with no verified international operations.
rationale: Small bitcoin treasury company with no consumer brand; F1 sponsorship is very unlikely.
changed: Renamed from Volcon to Empery Digital in 2025

name: OPENLANE
desc: Runs digital wholesale used-vehicle marketplaces, including OPENLANE and TradeRev, for dealers and commercial sellers.
markets: Marketplaces serve dealers in the United States, Canada and Europe.
rationale: B2B marketplace with little consumer exposure; F1 could host dealer clients, but marketing spend is modest.
changed: Renamed from KAR Auction Services to OPENLANE

name: Power Solutions International
desc: Makes emissions-certified engines and power systems that run on natural gas, propane and other fuels for industrial and power customers.
markets: Based in the United States; sells to OEM customers, mostly in North America.
rationale: B2B engine maker with no consumer brand; F1 hospitality has little commercial link.

name: Slate Auto
desc: Is building a low-cost electric pickup that can be customised with body kits, backed by Jeff Bezos.
markets: US start-up preparing launch and production in Indiana; no verified international plans.
rationale: Pre-launch start-up with a lean marketing budget and a US-only plan; F1 fit is weak at this stage.

name: Constellium
desc: Produces rolled and extruded aluminium products for aerospace, automotive, packaging and other industries.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, North America and Asia.
rationale: B2B aluminium supplier with aerospace and auto customers; F1 could show lightweight materials, but consumer awareness is minimal.

name: Dealer Tire
desc: Cleveland company supplying tires, wheels and related services to automakers and their dealerships, according to Crunchbase.
markets: Based in the United States and serving automakers and dealers; further detail not confirmed.
rationale: B2B tire distributor with limited public information; F1 has little clear link to its customer base.

name: Fastned
desc: Operates solar-roofed fast charging stations for electric cars in the Netherlands and several other European countries.
markets: Charging stations in the Netherlands, Germany, the UK, Belgium, France, Switzerland and Denmark.
rationale: European charging brand with strong sustainability message; F1 reach is wide relative to its network, so fit is moderate.

name: GreenCell Mobility
desc: Operates electric buses for public transport authorities in Indian cities such as Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru.
markets: Operates electric buses under contract in Indian cities only; no verified overseas plans.
rationale: Domestic contract operator with little consumer brand; F1 offers weak commercial value.

name: Subaru Corporation
desc: Makes Subaru vehicles such as the Impreza, Forester, Outback, Crosstrek, WRX and BRZ, known for all-wheel drive.
markets: Sells mainly in North America, Japan, Australia and Europe; Toyota is a significant shareholder.
rationale: Performance-oriented car brand with motorsport heritage in rallying; F1 could add global profile, though its spend is modest.

name: Textainer
desc: Leases intermodal shipping containers, including standard dry containers, to shipping lines around the world.
markets: Leases containers to shipping lines worldwide; ownership and listing status not confirmed here.
rationale: B2B container lessor with no consumer brand; F1 has a limited link, though its logistics customers might suit hospitality.

name: Zipline International
hq: South San Francisco, California, United States
desc: Designs, makes and operates autonomous delivery drones carrying blood, medicines, groceries and other goods.
markets: Operates in the United States and in African countries such as Rwanda, Ghana and Nigeria.
rationale: Technology-led delivery brand with US and African operations; F1 could provide a technology showcase, though its marketing budget is modest.

name: Ford Motor Company
desc: Makes and sells Ford and Lincoln cars, trucks and SUVs, including the F-Series, Mustang and Bronco.
markets: Sells in North America, Europe, Asia-Pacific, South America and the Middle East and Africa.
rationale: Already an F1 partner through Red Bull Ford Powertrains; the brand uses F1 for performance and technology marketing.
f1: Partner of Red Bull Ford Powertrains and runs Ford Racing in F1

name: Bolt
desc: Runs a mobility and delivery platform offering ride-hailing, e-scooters, bikes, and food and grocery delivery.
markets: Operates in Europe, Africa and other regions, with ride-hailing in many countries.
rationale: Consumer app brand seeking global awareness and drivers; F1 could suit market-entry campaigns in new regions.

name: Toyota Motor Credit Corporation
desc: Offers retail and lease financing, insurance and related services to Toyota and Lexus customers and dealers in the United States.
markets: Finance arm serving Toyota and Lexus customers and dealers in the United States.
rationale: Captive finance arm with no separate consumer marketing; F1 relevance comes through parent Toyota, not this entity.
f1: Subsidiary of Toyota, backer of Toyota Gazoo Racing and title partner of Haas F1

name: Bapcor
desc: Distributes automotive aftermarket parts across Australia and New Zealand, with retail and trade networks.
markets: Operates in Australia and New Zealand, with some Asian operations.
rationale: Parts distributor with local retail brands; F1 fit is limited to Australian motorsport interest.

name: ChargePoint
desc: Operates a large electric vehicle charging network, selling charging stations, software and subscriptions to businesses, fleets and drivers.
markets: Sells in North America and Europe through business customers, fleets and networked charging stations.
rationale: Charging brand with technology credentials and sites in the US and Europe; F1 could build awareness, but finances are tight.

name: Gates Industrial
desc: Makes power transmission belts, fluid power hoses and couplings for automotive, industrial and other customers.
industry: power transmission and fluid power maker
markets: Sells belts and hoses to industrial and automotive customers across the Americas, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B component maker with motorsport-adjacent engineering image; F1 could provide customer hospitality, though consumer brand awareness is low.

name: Knorr-Bremse
desc: Makes braking systems and safety technologies for rail vehicles and commercial vehicles.
industry: rail and truck braking systems maker
markets: Sells to rail and truck makers and operators across Europe, the Americas and Asia.
rationale: B2B braking specialist with engineering credentials; F1 hospitality may suit customers, but consumer awareness and relevance are limited.

name: Standard Motor Products
hq: Long Island City, New York, United States
desc: Makes and distributes replacement parts for vehicles, such as ignition, fuel system, emissions and temperature control products.
markets: Sells mainly in North America, with operations in Europe and Asia.
rationale: Aftermarket parts brand sold through retailers; F1 has limited link to its mostly North American customers.

name: BorgWarner
desc: Supplies powertrain and propulsion technologies including turbochargers, transmissions, thermal systems and electric vehicle components.
markets: Plants and customers across North America, Europe and Asia supplying major carmakers.
rationale: B2B supplier with turbo and electrification technology that fits motorsport engineering showcases; limited consumer brand.

name: Michelin
desc: Makes Michelin, BFGoodrich and Kleber tires, plus maps, guides and the Michelin Guide restaurant ratings.
markets: Sells tires and services across Europe, the Americas, Asia and Africa through dealers and carmaker supply.
rationale: Global tire brand with deep motorsport heritage and premium positioning; strong fit for hospitality and technology marketing.

name: Autobahn Tank & Rast Holding
desc: Operates most motorway service areas in Germany, with about 400 fuel stations and 50 hotels with restaurants, shops and charging.
markets: Operates on the German Autobahn only; owned by investors including Allianz and Borealis.
rationale: Domestic roadside concession operator with a modest brand; F1 fit is limited, though German motorists are a large audience.

name: AutoNation
desc: Retails new and used vehicles through more than 240 franchised new vehicle dealerships, with parts, service and financing.
markets: Dealerships in the United States only; no verified expansion plans outside the country.
rationale: Large US dealer group with some brand marketing; F1 relevance is limited by its domestic footprint.

name: Bajaj Auto International Holdings
desc: Holds the Bajaj Auto stake in the Austrian KTM group, owner of KTM, Husqvarna and GasGas motorcycle brands.
markets: Austrian holding of Bajaj Auto, which owns control of the KTM group selling motorcycles worldwide.
rationale: Holding vehicle without its own consumer brand; motorcycle brands could use motorsport, but F1 is a weak match.

name: Bridgestone Corporation
desc: Makes Bridgestone, Firestone and Dayton tires and rubber products, as the largest tire and rubber maker by revenue.
markets: Sells tires in the Americas, Europe, Asia and Africa through retail, dealers and carmaker supply.
rationale: Global tire brand with motorsport history and strong B2B and consumer reach; F1 offers brand visibility and customer hospitality.

name: KLA
desc: Makes process control and yield management equipment used in semiconductor manufacturing, including inspection and metrology systems.
markets: Sells to chipmakers across North America, Asia and Europe.
rationale: B2B equipment maker with a technology brand; F1 could offer hospitality and engineering showcase, but there is little consumer relevance.

name: Octopus Electric Vehicles
desc: Offers salary sacrifice, leasing and advice for electric vehicles as the car business of Octopus Energy Group.
markets: Serves customers in the United Kingdom only; no verified expansion plans abroad.
rationale: UK EV leasing brand with a sustainability focus and a growing consumer base; F1 relevance is modest and domestic.

name: Spinny
desc: Runs an Indian used-car platform where customers buy, sell and finance quality-checked pre-owned cars.
markets: Operates in Indian cities only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Fast-growing Indian consumer brand with heavy advertising; F1 fits its youth audience, but all customers are in India.

name: Splend
desc: Provides vehicle subscription and rental to gig economy drivers working for ride-hailing and delivery platforms.
markets: Serves drivers in Australia; no verified expansion beyond Australia.
rationale: Niche gig-driver rental service with limited marketing scale; F1 fit is weak.

name: Agora Data
desc: Provides an AI-driven data and credit platform for subprime auto lenders and dealers to price risk and originate loans.
markets: US fintech serving subprime auto lenders and dealers; no verified international customers.
rationale: B2B niche platform with no consumer awareness; F1 offers little strategic fit.

name: Fleetio
desc: Provides fleet management software for vehicle maintenance, inspections, fuel tracking and reporting.
markets: US software company serving fleet operators; international customers not confirmed.
rationale: B2B software brand with fleet customers; F1 could provide hospitality, but there is limited brand marketing or global reach.

name: Gestamp
desc: Makes metal components and structural parts for cars, such as body-in-white, chassis and mechanisms.
markets: Plants and customers across Europe, the Americas and Asia supplying most major carmakers.
rationale: B2B supplier with engineering and lightweighting credentials; F1 hospitality could support carmaker relationships, but consumer visibility is low.

name: Robo.ai
desc: Mobility and robotics technology company in Dubai providing electric vehicle, logistics and autonomous mobility services, per Crunchbase.
markets: Based in Dubai; products, customers and any international activity are not confirmed.
rationale: Little verified information; Gulf-based technology brand may want visibility, but scale and ownership are unclear.

name: TIER Mobility
desc: Rents e-scooters, e-bikes and mopeds in European cities through an app, now operating after merging with Dott.
markets: Operates in many European cities under TIER and Dott brands; backed by investors including SoftBank and Mubadala.
rationale: Consumer micromobility app with city-level exposure in Europe; F1 reach is wide but spend is hard to justify.

name: Voi Technology
desc: Runs shared e-scooters and e-bikes in more than 100 European cities, rented through an app.
markets: Operates in the Nordics, UK, Germany, Italy, Spain and other European cities under city licences.
rationale: Consumer brand with strong visibility in European cities and a young urban audience; F1 fit is moderate.

name: JAC Motors
desc: Builds light, medium and heavy trucks, passenger cars, buses and engines, including electric models and a venture with Volkswagen.
markets: Sells in China and exports to Latin America, the Middle East, Africa and Asia.
rationale: State-owned commercial and passenger vehicle maker with export markets; F1 relevance limited by value positioning.

name: Lizy
desc: Provides digital vehicle leasing to businesses and self-employed professionals in Belgium through a fully online process.
markets: Serves customers in Belgium only; no verified expansion plans.
rationale: Local fintech and leasing brand with Belgian customers; F1 audience is mostly outside its market.

name: Niron Magnetics
desc: Develops permanent magnets made from iron nitride, a rare-earth-free alternative for motors and other uses.
markets: US start-up with pilot production; planned commercial plant; customers and international plans not confirmed.
rationale: Pre-commercial materials start-up with a motor and EV technology story; F1 could serve as a showcase, but resources are limited.

name: Also
desc: Develops lightweight electric micromobility vehicles, such as the TM-B electric bike, as a spin-out from Rivian.
markets: Based in California with initial sales focused on the United States.
rationale: Early-stage consumer brand still building awareness; F1 could help technology credentials, but its marketing budget is small.
changed: Launched in 2024 as a Rivian spin-out

name: Canada Cartage
desc: Provides dedicated fleet, truckload freight and warehousing services for retail, grocery and industrial customers in Canada and the US.
markets: Serves customers across Canada and the United States.
rationale: B2B logistics firm with little consumer awareness; F1 hospitality might help customer relations, but fit is weak.

name: Dorman Products
desc: Supplies aftermarket automotive replacement parts, including hard-to-find parts, to retailers and professional repairers.
markets: US-based supplier selling mainly through North American retailers and distributors.
rationale: Aftermarket parts brand with motorsport-adjacent customers; its North American focus limits fit with global F1.

name: TMD Friction
desc: Makes brake pads, linings and friction materials under brands including Textar, Don and Mintex for carmakers and aftermarket.
markets: Plants in Europe, Asia and the Americas supplying carmakers, rail, industry and aftermarket customers.
rationale: B2B brake supplier with brands known to mechanics; F1 could suit brand and aftermarket marketing, but it competes with established brake partners.

name: WM Motor
desc: Was a Chinese electric vehicle maker that sold the EX5 SUV and W6 under the Weltmeister brand.
markets: Sold cars in China before filing for bankruptcy reorganisation in 2023; no ongoing production.
rationale: Company collapsed in 2023 and no longer sells cars; not a viable prospect for sponsorship.

name: GAC Aion New Energy Automobile
desc: Electric vehicle company of GAC Group, selling Aion S, Y and V models and the Hyper premium brand.
markets: Sells in China and exports to Southeast Asia, the Middle East, Europe and Latin America.
rationale: State-backed EV brand growing abroad with strong Chinese awareness; F1 could build exposure in export markets.

name: BeyonCa
desc: Beijing-based maker of electric vehicles with advanced features, according to Crunchbase; further details unconfirmed.
markets: Based in Beijing; models, owners and sales not confirmed; no verified international activity.
rationale: Little verified information; no known marketing activity or global brand to support an F1 case.
